en: Certain bamboo species can grow up to 91 centimeters in a single day, making them the fastest-growing plants on Earth.
A blue whale's heart weighs approximately 180 kilograms, which is roughly the same weight as a standard grand piano.
The Arctic tern migrates up to 70,000 kilometers annually, flying between the Arctic and Antarctic poles.
The human body produces about two million red blood cells every single second to constantly replace aging ones.
A human baby is born with around 270 bones, but adults only have 206 because several bones fuse together.
A single hectare of the Amazon rainforest can contain over 1,000 different species of beetles.
Periodical cicadas spend exactly 13 or 17 years underground as nymphs before finally emerging as winged adults.
A ruby-throated hummingbird's heart can beat up to 1,200 times per minute while it is hovering in flight.
A single orchid seed pod can produce up to four million tiny, dust-like seeds for reproduction.
A saltwater crocodile generates a bite force of over 3,700 pounds, the strongest measured bite of any living animal.
If uncoiled, the DNA inside just one single human cell would stretch out to about two meters long.
The eye of a giant squid can measure up to 27 centimeters across, which is the size of a basketball.
